text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press at the weekend. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL

- Israeli military equipment company Elbit Ltd. signed $100 million deal to upgrade Romania's 40 Puma helicopters. Elbit is currently working on a $300 million contract to upgrade the country's MiG 21 fleet by the year 2001.
- Some 70,000 Romanians will vote in Israel, 25,000 in the United States and 15,000 in neighbouring Hungary.

- Romania can solve its currency market crisis if it allows a slight but realistic depreciation of the leu, Henry Russell, representative of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development in Romania said in an interview.
- Government to debate 1997 state budget bill next week.
- Local car maker Automobile Dacia Pitesti produced 74,000 cars in the first 10 months of 1996 and estimated end-year production at 90,000 units.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Communications Ministry postponed announcing the successful bidders in the tender for two lucrative GSM licences.
- Romania will need sugar imports, as production is estimated at 260,000 tonnes, while the annual domestic consumption is currently at 450,000 tonnes.
- Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu denied forecasts of a petrol price rise in the first term of 1997.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Private airline Dac Air started twice weekly flights from Bucharest to Athens, with a stop in Timisoara, operated by CRJ jet aircraft.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Council of Europe's parliamentary assembly sent four observers to November 3 polls.

- Romania cannot become a full NATO member as long as structures of the former Securitate communist secret police still function, the newspaper says, quoting an unnamed official of the U.S. administration.
- The official also said the United States was unhappy about government pressure on journalists and their prosecution of two reporters for "defaming state authority".
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Recent press disclosure of a link between French Defence Minister Charles Hernu and the Securitate will have a negative impact on Romania's chances for NATO integration, newspaper says quoting comments in Bulgarian daily "24 Hours".
- Romanian state television is to broadcast IRSOP exit polls shortly after polling stations close on Sunday at midnight.
- Bulgarian border police caught two Turkish citizens who tried to smuggle 13.6 kg of heroin, hidden in the trunk of a car, over the border into Romania.
ADEVARUL
- Some six million ballots for presidential elections need to be reprinted because electoral logos of three independent candidates were not printed along with their names.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The Central Electoral Bureau is allowing journalists and observers to witness the vote counting process in polling stations.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Romania did not have a spy of such high level as French Defence Minister Charles Hernu, former Romanian ambassador to Washington and political analyst Silviu Brucan said.

- The newspaper reprints the outcome of 1992 presidential and parliament elections, when President Ion Iliescu got 47.3 percent of votes in the first round and 61.4 in run-off, with his main rival Emil Constantinescu getting 31.2 percent and then 38.6 percent.
ZIUA

- A full-page report on local and international protests to a court decision to sentence newspaper director Sorin Stanescu and reporter Tana Ardeleanu to jail terms for "defaming the state authority" -- allegations that President Iliescu had been a Soviet agent.

- The newspaper publishes an interview former Romanian security general and dissident Mihai Pacepa gave to the U.S.-based Romanian-language magazine Lumea Libera. He said the former Securitate played a leading role in installing the Soviet dictatorship in Romania and that Iliescu was part of Moscow plans for a coup to oust dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.

- The newspaper publishes the copy of a document it says shows that the leader of the ruling Party of Social Democracy leader Adrian Nastase had used up to nine billion lei of public money for his campaign starting April 1994. Nastase denies the charge, saying the documents were forged by the opposition.
AZI
- Romanians are to choose between change and stability on Sunday polls. ($=3,394 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
